verdict.rationale: Claude Design's own docs say it can apply a team's design system to every project automatically, and that a design system can be pulled in from Claude Code via /design-sync. That covers the cross-project sharing part of the story. Nothing describes publishing a library of components and styles across files, or a controlled process for reviewing and accepting updates when the source changes. The PenPot components a user built came from a different tool and earn no credit here. Missing for 10: explicit publishable shared libraries of components and styles, versioned or controlled update propagation when the source changes, per-file library linking, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a designer, shared libraries publish components and styles across files and projects, with controlled updates when the source changes

citations.quote: Claude can also apply your team's design system to every project automatically, so the output is consistent with the rest of your company's designs.
Pull in your design system from Claude Code using /design-sync
Import from GitHub, design files, or your local codebase so Claude can build with your real components.
